summary: Phase 149O.17 -- HATP Mandatory Production Consumption Implementation Plan: implementation-plan-only phase (zero src/pcae/** or contract changes). Ran the required initial inspection and confirmed baseline: repo clean, origin/main..HEAD=0, 149O.16.2 completed/complete, 149O.12B-Obs-PY39-1 independently confirmed resolved, HMRC-001 v1.0 VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS -- CONFORMS, HATP production NOT READY, runtime Observed/observe/unavailable. Read HMRC-001 (85 requirements, 14 security invariants MC-1..MC-14, 45-scenario attack matrix) and the 149O.14 architecture document in full, then independently re-confirmed the current real AG3 (execute_rollback -> _run_git_revert, agent.py:5234-5373) and AG5 (build_rollback_execution -> file write/unlink loop, agent.py:93952-94179) effect call graphs directly against live source (not against the architecture document's own reconstruction) -- both structurally unchanged since 149O.14, including the exact Wave-7 hook line numbers (agent.py:5238-5240, 93957-93959). Confirmed via direct source reading that HATPTrustStore.production().root (hatp_bootstrap.py:529,536) is already a public accessor to the existing Class-B protected trust root, meaning the new Cutover Record module needs no modification to hatp_bootstrap.py. Authored a complete implementation-ready plan (docs/PHASE_149O_17_HATP_MANDATORY_PRODUCTION_CONSUMPTION_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md) mapping all 85 HMRC-REQ requirements, all 14 MC invariants, and all 45 attack-matrix scenarios onto: a new hatp_mandatory_cutover.py module (Cutover Mode enum, Cutover Record schema/parser, protected storage reusing the existing trust root, a separate write-once monotonic-activation marker file resolving the first-install-vs-deleted-record ambiguity, mode-resolution algorithm with no caching, protected activation API with no public CLI); a new hatp_rollback_consumption.py module (explicit evidence-ID validation, HATPEvidenceStore.load, direct reuse of resolve_rollback_approval_evidence_with_hatp/verify_hatp_proof for approval derivation, and its own PB-request construction via two internal, non-caller-selectable entrypoints differing only in a hardcoded simulation_only value, resolving MC-14 without adding a caller-controllable truthfulness parameter to the existing, deliberately-unmodified hatp_ag_authority.py); precise per-branch modifications to core/agent.py's two effect functions (mode-dependent gating placed immediately before _run_git_revert/the file-write loop, preserving every existing structural precondition unconditionally, explicit per-parameter Wave-7 raw-hook disposition;) and CLI/commands/agent.py plumbing (--hatp-evidence-id flag, mode-dependent pcae remote rollback approve disposition). Explicitly designed the MC-14 effect-truthful PB path to construct a truthful simulation_only=False request for a real effect and documented that this is expected to resolve DENY under the current runtime posture (POL-005/COMP-002 unchanged, no workaround planned or implemented). Derived a six-wave implementation split (149O.18A: cutover-state foundation: 18B: consumption adapter; 18C/18D: AG3/AG5 effect-boundary integration via direct-call testing before any CLI wiring; 18E: CLI plumbing + legacy migration surfaces; 18F: assembled attack-matrix + activation-readiness integration) plus a reserved 149O.19 independent-verification phase, from first-principles dependency analysis (not by trusting the governing prompt's suggested split blindly) -- confirmed each wave is independently testable without activating mandatory mode on any real deployment and that no wave can break an existing LEGACY_COMPATIBLE deployment. Recorded 11 explicit implementation stop conditions covering the corrupt-record-with-no-marker edge case, Class-B monotonic-write-once assumptions, new-authority-timestamp parsing, raw-hook removal blast radius, effect-boundary caller-inventory completeness, PB-request structural-derivation sufficiency, and PREPARED->LEGACY_COMPATIBLE ambiguity (deliberately left unimplemented rather than guessed). Recorded one informational, non-numbered editorial observation: HMRC-001 Section 28's Threat Model header line informally re-uses the HMRC-REQ-080 label already normatively defined in Section 30; independently confirmed this does not contradict 149O.16's mechanical 85-unique-ID finding (149O.16's extraction pattern required an immediate trailing period, which the Section 28 citation does not have) -- recorded so 149O.19 does not rediscover it as a false new defect. Authored a mechanical, marker-based planning-completeness test (tests/test_phase_149o_17_hmrc_implementation_plan_completeness.py, 16 tests) that parses the plan document's own tables programmatically -- not by trusting its prose -- to confirm exactly 85/14/45 requirement/invariant/attack rows with no gaps or duplicates, cross-checks the 85-requirement and 45-attack counts against a fresh, independent mechanical extraction of HMRC-001's own contract text, confirms every planned production file appears in the file-ownership matrix, and confirms zero src/pcae/** changes and byte-identity for all seven contracts via two independently-implemented git-diff extraction methods. Ran the full repository-wide Fast Green suite (pytest -m fast_green): 5193 passed, 2 failed, 1 skipped on the raw run -- both failures are the exact same two pre-existing, unrelated failures 149O.16.2 already independently confirmed and disposed of via git-stash A/B (an environmental Python-interpreter-version assumption in test_phase_149o_13_...py, and a stale phase-entry-commit assumption in test_phase_149o_16_...py that is expected to go stale as later phases legitimately touch src/pcae/); this phase reconfirms both are still present and unrelated to this phase's own (docs/tests-only) changes, and did not need to re-run git-stash A/B itself since 149O.16.2 already established their root causes and disposition without new information changing that analysis. Fast Green with those two pre-existing failures deselected: 5193 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped -- zero new failures, and the 16-test delta (5177 -> 5193) is exactly this phase's own new planning-completeness test file. VERDICT: HATP MANDATORY PRODUCTION CONSUMPTION IMPLEMENTATION PLAN: COMPLETE -- READY FOR BOUNDED IMPLEMENTATION. No production source or contract was modified. No Cutover Record, consumption adapter, AG3/AG5 gate, or PB enforcement capability was implemented or activated. HMRC-001 v1.0 and all six upstream contracts remain byte-unchanged. B-149O-1..4 remain INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED AT HATP-GATED AUTHORITY BOUNDARY -- SYSTEM EXECUTION CLOSURE DEFERRED. HATP production remains NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable. Recommended next phase: 149O.18A -- HATP Mandatory Cutover State Foundation.
